provenance.l: Apollo 16 Mission Report (Tables 3-I and 3-V, sections 3.2 to 3.4): range zero 17:54:00 GMT 1972-04-16. A direct rendezvous (no CSI or CDH): vernier 10 ft/s at 175:42:18 (no duration in the sources read: 8 s is an estimate), TPI 176:26:05 (2.5 s, 78.0 ft/s on the LM computer, OCR of Table 3-V; 78.5 on the CM computer), TPF 177:08:42 (no duration or delta-V read: 25 s is an estimate). Quote: "inserted into a 40-mile by 8-mile lunar orbit about 7 minutes later ... a vernier adjustment maneuver of 10 ft/sec was necessary". Orbit 40.2 x 7.9 n.mi (OCR of Table 3-V; the text says 40 by 8); ascent 427.8 s (SP-4029; the MR table prints 427.7) and 6,054.2 ft/s (OCR); CSM 64.6 x 55.0 n.mi after the 169:05:52 plane change (OCR); docking 177:41:18; ascent stage jettison 195:00:12, attitude control lost, no deorbit: "Attitude control of the lunar module was lost at jettison; consequently, a deorbit maneuver was not possible."; subsatellite release 196:02:09 (without the planned orbit-shaping burn); TEI 200:21:33.07, 162.29 s, 3,370.9 ft/s. All times are the mission report / SP-4029 clock; entry compilation figures are in the splashdown profile

NASA SP-4029 Apollo 16 timeline: GET and GMT of liftoff, docking, jettison, the SIM bay door and the subsatellite events. Apollo 16 SIM bay: door jettisoned 069:59:01 (MR16 Table 3-I); the mass-spectrometer boom was jettisoned at 195:23:12 (not drawn); the subsatellite was launched at 196:02:09 into a short-life orbit, tracking lost on revolution 425 (29 May 1972)
